title: fix(plugins): report consistent third-party npm installs accurately
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #175429: a consistent third-party npm plugin install is reported as `provenance-invalid`, prompting a reinstall that cannot change its catalog status.

Supersedes #175451, thanks @LiuwqGit.

## User Impact

Inspection reports `third-party-npm` for consistent, non-catalog npm installs. Explicitly allowed plugins no longer produce the unverified-install warning, and hook-turn refusals explain that reinstalling the same package cannot grant official trust. Trust eligibility is unchanged; conflicting identities, local artifacts, official-ID namesakes, and catalog packages recorded under another ID retain their existing classifications.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared install-record classifier conflated valid third-party provenance with invalid official provenance. Reuse the existing npm identity parser and catalog checks to distinguish them at that owner. Keep all trust-gated capability decisions unchanged. Remove a one-use official-name helper and simplify identity collection and redundant temporary control flow in the same owner.

Release-note context: correct third-party npm diagnostics in plugin inspection, Gateway warnings, and hook-turn refusals; fixes #175429; thanks @LiuwqGit.

## Evidence

- Base `57a5d82a831e26963dc470b521a4b3dd1e0665b6`: new loader regression fails with expected `third-party-npm`, received `provenance-invalid`; 13 other cases pass.
- Node: 158 tests pass across six files, including loader/inspection, install-record identity, Gateway trust refusal, Doctor registry repair, missing-plugin repair, and the matching tooling consumer.
- Bun (pinned OpenClaw runtime): the same 158 tests pass. Total wrapper time: Node 80.65s, Bun 76.21s. The loader file used about 8.24s / 6.91s of test time; the install-record unit file used 2ms / 3ms.
- Live: used the real built CLI with the pinned Bun runtime, an isolated HOME/state/profile and free port, and a synthetic npm registry package declaring startup activation. Initial install and reinstall of `trust-probe-plugin@1.0.0` both returned `third-party-npm`; the Gateway logged `http server listening (2 plugins: memory-core, trust-probe; 1.5s)` with zero unverified-install warnings and shut down cleanly. The fixture runs the real npm installer and durable registry, with no contributor code. Native Node CLI proof was blocked because the host has Node 26.12.0 and the CLI requires 26.12.1; Node tests passed and live proof used supported Bun. An initial fixture omitted startup activation and was corrected before claiming startup proof.
- Scoped plugin-platform typecheck (`node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.plugins-platform.json --incremental`), type-aware oxlint on the five TypeScript files, oxfmt on all six changed files, and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-madge-import-cycles.ts` pass; 0 import cycles.
- Commands: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <six consumer test files> --maxWorkers=1` with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node` and `bun`; live commands were `openclaw.mjs --profile <isolated-profile> plugins install npm:trust-probe-plugin@1.0.0 --force --accept-capabilities`, `plugins inspect trust-probe --runtime --json`, and `gateway run --allow-unconfigured --bind loopback --port <free-port> --auth none`.
- Independent Codex review: no actionable P0–P2 findings on the final diff.
- Production: +40/-40, net 0 lines. Tests: +56/-0. Docs: +1/-0. No schema, dependency, config-option, or CLI-option changes.
- The commit wrapper could not bootstrap pinned pnpm under its release-age policy. Ran the same Markdown lint configuration directly (0 issues), the configured staged-content guard, and the other focused checks before using the documented equivalent-check local-commit path.
- Full `check:changed` was not run because of the local SQLite-inventory time budget; scoped checks cover the touched surface, with PR CI providing broad validation. npm SLSA attestations and external registry availability are outside this change.
